title: the Yaksha's questions
hook: one by one the brothers go to the lake, each with his own strength, and each ignores the voice
carry: the lake wants to be answered

segments.voice: Yesterday: arani, the brahmin's fire-sticks, carried off by a deer, and Nakula, who drank before he listened. Your line was a brother who didn't wait to hear them.

Nakula doesn't come back. Under the tree, his brothers wait, and wait, and Yudhishthira sends the next one. Sahadeva, go and find your brother, and bring water. So Sahadeva follows the cranes to the lake, and there is Nakula, lying on the bank. Sahadeva is grieving, and burning with thirst, and the voice speaks again, the same words. This lake is mine. Answer first. Back under the tree, three brothers are still waiting for water.
screen: `NAKULA DOESN'T COME BACK.` → `SAHADEVA GOES NEXT.` → `THE SAME VOICE, THE SAME WORDS.`

segments.voice: Sahadeva drinks, and falls beside his brother. Now Yudhishthira sends Arjuna, the great archer. Arjuna reaches the lake with his bow ready and sees both twins dead. He looks around for an enemy and sees no one. When the voice speaks, Arjuna does what a warrior does. He shoots at it, sending arrows toward the sound, aiming by ear alone. The voice answers, unhurt: your arrows can't touch me. Answer my questions, and then drink. Arjuna drinks, and falls. Then Bhima comes, the strong one. He sees three brothers on the ground and decides this must be the work of some spirit, and that he'll fight whoever it is. But first, water. The voice warns him too. He doesn't listen. He drinks, and falls. Notice what each one brings. Nakula brings his thirst. Sahadeva brings his grief. Arjuna brings an archer's aim. Bhima brings his strength, and a plan to fight. Not one of them brings what the voice asked for: a moment to listen, and an answer. The lake doesn't want to be conquered. It wants to be answered. Each brother meets it with his own best gift, and for this lake it's the wrong gift. Four heroes of the Mahabharata lie on a lakeshore because they wouldn't stop to hear a question. One brother is left.
screen: `SAHADEVA DRINKS, AND FALLS.` · `ARJUNA SHOOTS AT THE VOICE.` · `BHIMA PLANS TO FIGHT, BUT DRINKS.` · then, large: `IT WANTS TO BE ANSWERED.`

segments.voice: Close your eyes if you like, and let the sounds around you arrive: traffic, a fan, a voice in another room, your own breath. Notice how quickly the mind wants to aim at each one, name it and judge it, and instead let each sound come and go, unanswered and unshot. If you pray, you can rest in that listening as a kind of prayer.
Yaksha, the unseen spirit who owns the lake and asks a question before anyone may drink. Four brothers bring thirst, grief, aim and strength, and none of them stops to listen. Today's word.
Your line: the lake wants to be answered. Thirst, grief, aim and strength all came up short. Day eight hundred two, done.

howItsDone: In the epic, the four brothers fall one by one before Yudhishthira arrives, each warned by the same voice in the same words.

chat.meaning: The voice said his arrows couldn't touch it. The lake wanted to be answered, not conquered, and each brother brought the wrong gift.

notes: All paraphrase. Confirm in Ganguli the order Sahadeva, Arjuna, Bhima; Arjuna shooting toward the sound and the voice's reply that his arrows cannot harm it; Bhima's thought that this is the work of yakshas or rakshasas and his intent to fight after drinking.
